newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Interstar sets A$300 mln of mortgage backed debt.
newsitem.headline: Interstar sets A$300 mln of mortgage backed debt.

text.p: Australia's Interstar Securities Pty Ltd said on Friday it is making its first public offering of A$300 million of mortgaged-backed certificates.
Bankers Trust Australia and SBC Warburg Australia are co-lead managers, while J.B. Were Capital Markets acted in the capacity if programme adviser.

Interstar is one of Australia's largest independent mortgage lenders and in a statement issued by Bankers Trust it said that it is believed to be one of Australia's oldest mortgage orignator and securitisor.
Previous Interstar issues were privately placed with institutional investors.
IssueOne would be the initial A$300 million offering of certificates under the new Interstar RD25 Master Trust programme.

"The programme has been designed to maximise appeal for institutional investors allowing Interstar the flexibility to deal with its current strong orignation growth," said Vernon Spencer, Managing Director of Interstar.
"Interstar expects additional certificates to be issued under the RD25 Trust," he added.
All the certificates are floating securities and are to be sold to investors at par.
Pricing is expected to be June 30 at a margin over the 90 day bank bill swap rate (BBSW) and settlement is on July 2.
There are three tranches in the IssueOne transaction, A$190 million in Class A2 certificates, A$80 million of Class A3 and A$30 million of Class B.
All Class A certificates rank pari passu, while Class B are subordinated to all Class A Certificates,
The Class A certificates are rated AAA by Standard & Poor's and the Class B AA minus.
All certificates have been issued with optional redemption call dates and a corresponding step up in coupon rates.
During the initial 24 months following this issue no principal is expected to be repaid to investors, thereafter allocated principal will be applied sequentially to redeem each class of certificates.

If principal funds available to the Trust are insufficient to allow a redraw, or to allow for the approval of a further advance, the Trust may issue Class A1 certificates, which if issued will also be rated AAA and rank pari passu.

"Investors seeking a high quality and flexible investment should find this tranched Interstar structure very attractive. Interstar has a long track record of originating quality mortgages and this is reflected in the characteristics of the pool of mortgages," said Adrian Bentley, head of Bankers Trust Australia's Debt Finance.

"The diversity of this new name and structure, the high quality of the mortgages together with the robustness of the mortgage origniator and underwriting standards will create keen demand," added Robert Lempriere, of SBC Warburg.
